module.name: fpcasan
module.short: Run time support and annotations for AddressSanitizer (-fsanitize=address)

descr.p: fpcasan is the run time part of the -fsanitize=address compiler option (x86_64-linux, native code generator). The compiler adds the unit to every module compiled with the option: it links libasan and contains the trampolines FPC_ASAN_READ and FPC_ASAN_WRITE that the instrumented code calls before each memory access. The trampolines check the shadow memory of AddressSanitizer themselves and preserve all general purpose registers, the flags and xmm0..xmm15; a bad access is reported with the stack of the program and stops it.

Heap blocks are allocated by cmem, which the compiler adds to the program, so that AddressSanitizer surrounds them with red zones and detects heap buffer overflows, use-after-free, double frees and, at exit, memory leaks. Accesses to local and global variables are not checked.
Custom allocators that keep freed blocks (pools, free lists) can mark them with and , guarded by the FPC_SANITIZE_ADDRESS conditional define that the option sets.
On other platforms the routines are empty.

element.name: AsanPoison
element.short: Marks a memory range as not addressable

descr.p: AsanPoison calls __asan_poison_memory_region: a later instrumented access to the range is reported as an error, like an access to freed heap memory. Call it when a custom allocator takes a block back into its pool.
AddressSanitizer tracks addressability in 8-byte granules: a range that does not start at a multiple of 8 bytes may be poisoned only partly.

element.name: AsanPoison.aSize
element.short: Size of the range in bytes

element.name: AsanUnpoison
element.short: Marks a memory range as addressable again

descr.p: AsanUnpoison calls __asan_unpoison_memory_region. Call it when a custom allocator hands a block out of its pool again.

element.name: AsanUnpoison.aSize
element.short: Size of the range in bytes

element.name: AsanIsPoisoned
element.short: Tells whether an access to a memory range would be reported

descr.p: AsanIsPoisoned returns True when some byte of the range is not addressable (__asan_region_is_poisoned), and always False when the program does not run under AddressSanitizer.

element.name: AsanIsPoisoned.Result
element.short: True if an instrumented access to the range would be an error

element.name: AsanIsPoisoned.aSize
element.short: Size of the range in bytes
